## 1. Command Structure: `/community-manage`

Main command that orchestrates the entire workflow.

### Command Definition

File: `.claude/commands/community-manage.md`

```yaml
---
name: community-manage
description: Automate community management across all channels
args:
  channels: Comma-separated channels or "all" (default all)
  mode: "monitor" (read-only) or "respond" (auto-respond enabled)
  escalation_threshold: Complexity score 1-10 for human escalation (default 7)
---

# Community Management Automation

You are orchestrating community monitoring, triage, and response.

## Input Parameters

- **channels**: {{channels}} (twitter, linkedin, instagram, facebook, email, discord, slack)
- **mode**: {{mode}} (monitor=read-only, respond=auto-respond enabled)
- **escalation_threshold**: {{escalation_threshold}} (1-10, higher=more escalations)

## Execution Flow

### Phase 1: Monitoring & Collection

Execute `/community-monitor {{channels}}` to collect messages from:
- Social platforms (Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook)
- Email inboxes (support@, hello@, contact@)
- Chat systems (Discord, Slack, Intercom)

Expected output: 200-500 messages from last 24 hours.

### Phase 2: Triage & Classification

Execute `/community-triage {{messages}}` to:
- Categorize by type (Support, Sales, Feedback, Complaint, Compliment, Spam)
- Assign priority (P0, P1, P2, P3)
- Calculate complexity score (1-10)

Expected output: Categorized & prioritized messages with scores.

### Phase 3: Response or Escalation

Execute `/community-respond {{triaged_messages}} {{mode}} {{escalation_threshold}}` to:
- Auto-respond to simple messages (complexity < threshold)
- Escalate complex messages to human review
- Enforce response quality checks
- Send responses to channels or create tickets

Expected output: 200+ messages processed, 70% auto-resolved, 30% escalated.

### Phase 4: Analytics & Reporting

Generate daily report:
- Messages processed: [count]
- Auto-responded: [count] ([%])
- Escalated: [count] ([%])
- Average response time (auto): [minutes]
- Average response time (human): [minutes]
- Sentiment distribution: [breakdown]
- Top 5 issues detected: [list]
- Time saved vs manual: [hours]

## Success Criteria

- ✅ 100% of messages categorized
- ✅ 60-70% auto-responded (in respond mode)
- ✅ <5 minutes response time for P0/P1
- ✅ Zero spam in escalated messages
- ✅ Total time < 2 hours/day (vs 8+ hours manual)
- ✅ Sentiment trend tracked
- ✅ VIP customers prioritized
```

### Usage Examples

```bash
# Monitor all channels, read-only (no auto-responses)
/community-manage all monitor 7

# Full automation with default threshold
/community-manage all respond 7

# Only Twitter and LinkedIn, lower escalation threshold (more human review)
/community-manage twitter,linkedin respond 5

# High escalation threshold (more automation, less human review)
/community-manage all respond 9
```

## 2. Subcommand: `/community-monitor`

Collects messages from all channels in parallel.

File: `.claude/commands/community-monitor.md`

```yaml
---
name: community-monitor
description: Monitor and collect messages from all channels
args:
  channels: Target channels to monitor
---

# Community Monitoring Subcommand

Collect all unread/unanswered messages from the last 24 hours.

## Parallel Agents

### Agent 1: Social Media Monitor

Monitor Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook for:
- @mentions and replies
- Direct messages
- Comment threads
- Unread inbox

Data to extract:
```json
{
  "platform": "twitter",
  "message_id": "twitter_12345",
  "author": {
    "username": "customer_handle",
    "display_name": "Customer Name",
    "followers": 5000,

    "profile_url": "https://twitter.com/..."
  },
  "content": "How do I reset my password?",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-17T14:30:00Z",
  "type": "mention|dm|comment|quote",
  "engagement": {
    "likes": 2,
    "retweets": 0,

## 3. Batch Configuration

File: `.claude/config.yaml` (batch processing settings)

```yaml
community_management:
  # Batch processing
  batch:
    enabled: true
    wave_size: 20  # Process 20 messages per wave
    max_waves_parallel: 5  # Run up to 5 waves in parallel
    max_total_messages: 500  # Max messages per batch
    error_recovery: true

  # Timing
  schedules:
    morning_batch:
      time: "08:00"
      timezone: "America/New_York"
    afternoon_batch:
      time: "12:00"
    evening_batch:
      time: "16:00"
    overnight:
      time: "20:00"
      escalations_only: true

  # Channels
  monitors:
    twitter:
      enabled: true
      api: "twitter_api"
      check_interval: 15  # minutes
    linkedin:
      enabled: true
      api: "linkedin_api"
      check_interval: 30
    instagram:
      enabled: true
      api: "instagram_graph"
      check_interval: 30
    facebook:
      enabled: true
      api: "facebook_graph"
      check_interval: 30
    email:
      enabled: true
      inboxes: ["support@", "hello@", "contact@"]
      check_interval: 10
    discord:
      enabled: true
      check_interval: 5
    slack:
      enabled: true
      check_interval: 5

  # Auto-response
  auto_response:
    enabled: true
    complexity_threshold: 7  # 1-10, < threshold = auto-respond
    quality_check: true
    validate_links: true

  # Escalation
  escalation:
    enabled: true
    slack_channel: "#community-escalations"
    email_notif: "manager@company.com"
    sla:
      P0: 1  # hour
      P1: 4
      P2: 24
      P3: 48

  # Analytics
  analytics:
    track_sentiment: true
    track_response_time: true
    track_resolution_rate: true
    daily_report: true
    report_time: "17:30"
    report_email: "team@company.com"
```

## 4. Message Analysis Agent

Real agent prompt for analyzing and categorizing messages.

### Categorizer Agent Prompt

```markdown
# Message Categorizer Agent

You analyze community messages and categorize them by type.

## Your Task

For each message, determine:
1. **Category** (required): Support, Sales, Feedback, Complaint, Compliment, Spam
2. **Confidence**: 0.0-1.0 (how sure you are)
3. **Keywords**: 3-5 relevant words
4. **Entities**: Product, feature, or component mentioned

## Categories

### Support
- User asking how to do something
- Technical problem they're experiencing
- Questions about features or functionality
- Need help with account/setup

Examples:
- "How do I reset my password?"
- "The export button isn't working"
- "Can I use this with Zapier?"

### Sales
- Asking about pricing
- Feature inquiry
- Comparison with competitors
- Demo request
- Free trial questions

Examples:
- "How much does the Pro plan cost?"
- "Do you support API integrations?"
- "Can I schedule a demo?"

### Feedback
- Feature request
- Suggestion for improvement
- Product idea
- Workflow enhancement

Examples:
- "I wish you had dark mode"
- "It would be great if we could bulk export"
- "Would love to see Slack integration"

### Complaint
- Negative experience
- Bug report
- Dissatisfaction
- Problem not resolved

Examples:
- "Your app keeps crashing on my phone"
- "I've been waiting 3 days for support response"
- "This is way too expensive for what it does"

### Compliment
- Positive feedback
- Appreciation
- Thank you message
- Praise for feature/service

Examples:
- "Love your product! Best decision ever"
- "Thanks for the quick response!"
- "Your customer service is amazing"

### Spam
- Unrelated promotional content
- Bot messages
- Phishing attempts
- Duplicate spam
- Irrelevant links

Examples:
- "BUY NOW - Get rich quick!"
- "Check out my course: [unrelated link]"
- Automated bot response

## Analysis Instructions

For each message:

1. **Read** the content carefully
2. **Extract** key intent clues (question marks, imperative verbs, sentiment words)
3. **Match** against category definitions above
4. **Check** for multiple possible categories (assign primary + secondary if applicable)
5. **Rate** your confidence (0.0-1.0)

## Output Format

```json
{
  "message_id": "msg_001",
  "primary_category": "support",
  "secondary_category": null,
  "confidence": 0.95,
  "reasoning": "Contains 'How do I' + technical issue",
  "keywords": ["password", "reset", "account"],
  "entities": {
    "product": "Authentication",
    "feature": "Password reset",
    "issue_type": "how_to"
  }
}
```

## Edge Cases

- **Multi-category**: Pick PRIMARY category based on main intent. List secondary if equally important.
- **Unclear**: Rate confidence 0.6-0.7. Include explanation.
- **Context needed**: If you need customer history, note it in reasoning.

---

Input messages:
```
1. "Hi, I forgot my password. How do I reset it?"
   → Support, confidence 0.98, keywords: password, reset, how

6. "Is there a free trial?"

## 5. Auto-Moderation Rules

File: `.claude/rules/moderation-rules.yaml`

```yaml
moderation:
  # Spam filtering
  spam_detection:
    keywords:
      block_list:
        - "buy now"
        - "click here"
        - "limited time"
        - "get rich"
        - "free money"
        - "viagra"
        - "casino"
        - "lottery"
        - "inheritance"
        - "nigerian prince"

      suspicious_list:
        - "check this out"
        - "make money fast"
        - "click link"
        - "dm for details"

    phishing_patterns:
      - "verify your account"
      - "confirm password"
      - "click here to activate"
      - "unusual activity detected"
      - "update payment method"

    link_ratio:
      max_links_per_message: 3
      action: "mark_spam"

  # Hateful content & policy violations
  content_policy:
    blocked_patterns:
      - "slurs|hate_speech|harassment"
      - "threats|violence|illegal"
      - "doxxing|personal_info"

    escalation: "flag_for_human_review"
    action: "remove_and_notify_author"

  # Duplicate detection
  deduplication:
    enabled: true
    check_exact_match: true
    check_semantic_similarity: true
    similarity_threshold: 0.85
    action: "keep_first_remove_copies"

  # Blocklist management
  blocklist:
    sources:
      - "manual_blocks"
      - "spam_repeat_offenders"
      - "abuse_reports"

    auto_block_criteria:
      spam_messages_in_24h: 5
      action: "auto_block_account"

  # Response rate limiting
  rate_limiting:
    per_user_per_hour: 10  # Max 10 messages per user per hour
    per_user_per_day: 50   # Max 50 messages per user per day
    action: "flag_for_review"

  # Escalation rules
  escalation:
    very_negative_sentiment: true
    escalate_to_human: "immediately"

    vip_customer: true
    escalate_to_senior: true

    mentions_outage: true
    escalate_to_engineering: true
```

## 6. Engagement Scoring Algorithm

Calculate engagement priority for each customer/message.

```python
def calculate_engagement_score(message: dict, customer: dict) -> float:
    """
    Calculate engagement priority score (0-100).
    Higher = more important to respond quickly.

    Factors:
    - Customer LTV (Lifetime Value)
    - Message urgency (sentiment + category)
    - Customer influence (followers on social)
    - Account tenure
    - Churn risk
    """

    score = 0.0

    # 1. Customer value (0-30 points)
    ltv = customer.get('lifetime_value', 0)
    if ltv > 10000:
        score += 30  # Enterprise customer
    elif ltv > 5000:
        score += 25  # High-value customer
    elif ltv > 1000:
        score += 15  # Standard paying customer
    elif ltv > 0:
        score += 5   # Trial/free customer

    # 2. Message urgency (0-40 points)
    sentiment = message.get('sentiment', 'neutral')
    category = message.get('category', 'other')

    sentiment_score = {
        'very_negative': 40,
        'negative': 25,
        'neutral': 10,
        'positive': 5
    }.get(sentiment, 10)

    category_score = {
        'complaint': 35,
        'support': 25,
        'sales': 20,
        'feedback': 10,
        'compliment': 5,
        'spam': 0
    }.get(category, 15)

    # Use max to avoid double-counting negative sentiment + complaint
    score += max(sentiment_score, category_score)

    # 3. Customer influence (0-15 points)
    followers = message.get('author', {}).get('followers', 0)
    if followers > 100000:
        score += 15  # Major influencer
    elif followers > 50000:
        score += 12
    elif followers > 10000:
        score += 8
    elif followers > 1000:
        score += 3

    # 4. Account tenure (0-10 points)
    import datetime
    signup_date = customer.get('signup_date')
    if signup_date:
        days_active = (datetime.datetime.now() - signup_date).days
        if days_active > 365:
            score += 10  # Long-term customer
        elif days_active > 30:
            score += 5

    # 5. Churn risk (0-5 bonus points)
    if customer.get('churn_risk_score', 0) > 0.7:
        score += 5  # At-risk customer needs attention

    # Clamp to 0-100
    return min(100.0, max(0.0, score))


# Example usage:
message = {
    'id': 'msg_001',
    'content': 'Your app keeps crashing!',
    'sentiment': 'very_negative',
    'category': 'complaint',
    'author': {
        'username': 'influencer_user',
        'followers': 50000
    }
}

customer = {
    'email': 'vip@company.com',
    'lifetime_value': 15000,
    'signup_date': datetime.datetime(2022, 1, 1),
    'churn_risk_score': 0.8
}

score = calculate_engagement_score(message, customer)
print(f"Engagement score: {score}/100")  # Output: ~95 (very urgent)
```

## 7. Sentiment Analysis & Routing

Analyze sentiment and route to appropriate handler.

```python
def analyze_sentiment(text: str) -> dict:
    """
    Analyze sentiment of message.
    Returns: {sentiment, confidence, emotion_indicators}
    """

    # Sentiment keywords (simplified; use ML in production)
    very_negative = {
        'words': ['terrible', 'awful', 'useless', 'broken', 'hate', 'worst',
                  'disaster', 'disgusting', 'pathetic'],
        'patterns': ['will never', 'complete waste', 'refund', 'lawsuit']
    }

    negative = {
        'words': ['bad', 'poor', 'issue', 'problem', 'crash', 'disappointed',
                  'frustrated', 'unhappy', 'angry'],
        'patterns': ["doesn't work", 'not working', 'broken']
    }

    positive = {
        'words': ['great', 'love', 'awesome', 'excellent', 'perfect',
                  'amazing', 'thanks', 'appreciate', 'grateful'],
        'patterns': ['so helpful', 'best ever', 'highly recommend']
    }

    text_lower = text.lower()

    # Count matches
    very_neg_count = sum(1 for w in very_negative['words'] if w in text_lower)
    very_neg_count += sum(1 for p in very_negative['patterns'] if p in text_lower)

    neg_count = sum(1 for w in negative['words'] if w in text_lower)
    neg_count += sum(1 for p in negative['patterns'] if p in text_lower)

    pos_count = sum(1 for w in positive['words'] if w in text_lower)
    pos_count += sum(1 for p in positive['patterns'] if p in text_lower)

    # Determine sentiment
    if very_neg_count > 0:
        sentiment = 'very_negative'
        confidence = min(0.95, 0.7 + (very_neg_count * 0.1))
    elif neg_count > pos_count:
        sentiment = 'negative'
        confidence = 0.6 + (neg_count * 0.1)
    elif pos_count > 0:
        sentiment = 'positive'
        confidence = 0.6 + (pos_count * 0.1)
    else:
        sentiment = 'neutral'
        confidence = 0.5

    return {
        'sentiment': sentiment,
        'confidence': min(1.0, confidence),
        'indicators': {
            'very_negative_words': very_neg_count,
            'negative_words': neg_count,
            'positive_words': pos_count
        }
    }


def route_by_sentiment(message: dict) -> dict:
    """Route message based on sentiment analysis."""

    sentiment_analysis = analyze_sentiment(message['content'])
    routing = {
        'very_negative': {
            'priority': 'P0',
            'escalate': True,
            'route_to': 'senior_support_agent',
            'sla_minutes': 60
        },
        'negative': {
            'priority': 'P1',
            'escalate': False,
            'route_to': 'support_agent_or_escalation',
            'sla_minutes': 240
        },
        'neutral': {
            'priority': 'P2',
            'escalate': False,
            'route_to': 'support_agent_or_auto',
            'sla_minutes': 1440
        },
        'positive': {
            'priority': 'P3',
            'escalate': False,
            'route_to': 'acknowledge',
            'sla_minutes': 2880
        }
    }

    sentiment = sentiment_analysis['sentiment']
    routing_info = routing[sentiment]

    return {
        'sentiment_analysis': sentiment_analysis,
        'routing': routing_info,
        'priority': routing_info['priority'],
        'escalate': routing_info['escalate']
    }


# Example
message = {
    'id': 'msg_001',
    'content': 'Your app is terrible! It crashed and I lost all my data. This is a disaster!'
}

result = route_by_sentiment(message)
print(f"Sentiment: {result['sentiment_analysis']['sentiment']}")
# Output: very_negative → P0 → Escalate immediately to senior agent
```

## 10. Integration Example: Slack Escalation Notification

Example of what escalation notification looks like in Slack:

```json
{
  "type": "escalation_notification",
  "channel": "#community-escalations",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "header",
      "text": {
        "type": "plain_text",
        "text": "🚨 P1 Community Escalation",
        "emoji": true
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "*Customer:* Sarah Chen (@sarah_tech) | *Plan:* Enterprise | *LTV:* $15,000\n*Issue:* App keeps crashing on export\n*Sentiment:* 😡 Very Negative\n*Complexity:* 8/10"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "divider"
    },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "*Original Message:*\n> Your app is completely broken! Every time I try to export, it crashes. I've lost data THREE times now. This is unacceptable for an enterprise product. I want a refund or this needs fixed TODAY."
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "divider"
    },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "*Suggested Response:*\n> Hi Sarah, I'm deeply sorry to hear about this critical issue. This is absolutely unacceptable, and I understand your frustration. I'm immediately escalating this to our engineering team as P0.\n>\n> Can you please reply with: 1) Your OS/browser version 2) Steps to reproduce the crash\n>\n> I'll personally monitor this and follow up with you within 1 hour.\n>\n> Again, very sorry for the impact on your data."
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": {
            "type": "plain_text",
            "text": "Take Ownership"
          },
          "action_id": "escalation_take_ownership"
        },
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": {
            "type": "plain_text",
            "text": "Edit Response"
          },
          "action_id": "escalation_edit_response"
        },
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": {
            "type": "plain_text",
            "text": "View Full Context"
          },
          "action_id": "escalation_view_context"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "context",
      "elements": [
        {
          "type": "mrkdwn",
          "text": "⏰ SLA: 1 hour | 📊 Ticket: TICKET-5432 | 🔗 Twitter: [@sarah_tech](https://twitter.com/sarah_tech)"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
